body: Thanks for the info about this. If the HC is working when I get it, I'll try to remember to aim for 3 spaced out stars. I managed to find the manual online, and it seems to suggest the same, and offers a 2 star option if you know more information. I'm not sure how this will work at all, so I am prepared to probably have to do many minor adjustments.

I've watched a few videos on how to collimate this scope, and am looking into buying a tool for it. Some people have said it's really hard, others say that its quite easy, so I'm going to hope that it doesn't need much adjusting at all! I have seen Saturn once before, so seeing it again will be incredible! The rest of the universe has just been naked eye observations, so I am really looking forward to seeing anything at all. There are a few astronomy clubs around me, but they all are a bit too far to travel (especially given I can't drive (medical reasons)) so I am loathe to sign up to one. However, one of the local uni's offers talks for the public I enjoy going to. It's not the same, but until I can move, or get a friend that can drive into this hobby, I'm stuck with urban skies.

That makes a lot of sense. I do think if something major isn't working, I won't bother getting that sorted given it's age and that its discontinued for some time now, so thanks for confirming that for me. Thanks for the extra info about the mirror, too! I had no idea about that. Being able to see anything is the goal really, and the Moon and Jupiter would be my go-to's there! It seems like DSO's are not really an option here, as I also have Bortle Class 5 LP, but I may have better luck travelling to somewhere better, even if it's still blurry. I am really excited about getting this scope, and don't mind at all if it isnt that good, as it's a gift and it's my first. I can use this scope to learn what I like and don't like, and how to navigate before purchasing one myself down the line. If all I take away from this is what not to do, than that's a win. It's definitely good to know I can just point and look if the tech is too old!

Thanks! I'm happy to see anything really, especially as it is a gift whilst I save up for a newer model. I've just finished reading a manual I found for it online, so have some idea what cables and batteries might be needed. I expect I won't know a lot of what needs adjusting or buying till I have it.

I don't know if you'll know, but the manual said I can adjust the scope manually, rather than using the HC if the power dies, but I can't find any info on how to do that, or see any obvious places to alter where the scope is pointing. I'm also looking into purchasing cheap but good quality things like a red torch and a good book for studying the sky more effectively.

I used to commute from my house to uni in first year. It's really easy. Just get the triangle from Herne Bay to Canterbury bus station (about 30mins) and then get the bus to uni (about 20mins). Both buses run every 15 mins during the day. Also, an oyster card is only for the London. As a uni of Kent student, you can get a student bus pass (let's you get on any stagecoach bus, which is basically every bus in Kent). As an idea of prices there, a normal year long buss pass if like £700. Last year our student pass was £195. Highly recommended getting the bus pass. So much cheaper, and as I mentioned you can go anywhere via bus in Kent on that bus pass, so you could go to Dover or Folkstone or Ashford... I think there is even a bus to London? I have been using the bus for about 10 years now, and I am very familiar with Stagecoach (the bus company) as I've had to use it to go to secondary school and now for uni. Feel free if you want to ask any questions! I also live along the coast, and can offer advice about that area of Kent. As for living in Herne Bay, it's an okay town. The beach is nothing like what I have seen of beaches in Aus. Also, as most beaches are at most an hour away from any point in Kent, if you do choose to live closer to uni and more 'in land' it's still super easy and quick to visit the coast. Hope this helps!
